explanation: Track counts for the previous two prefixes. A nonzero final digit extends the previous prefix; a final pair from 10 through 26 extends the prefix before it. BigInteger preserves intermediate counts before the guaranteed int-sized final result.
timeComplexity: O(n) arithmetic operations for n digits; big-integer costs depend on intermediate count width.
spaceComplexity: Two BigInteger counts, using O(n) bits in the worst case.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A decoding of each prefix ends with either a valid nonzero single digit or a valid pair from 10 through 26. Removing that final token gives a decoding of the preceding one- or two-shorter prefix. Those cases are disjoint and exhaustive, so adding their counts yields exactly all decodings. Arbitrary-precision intermediate counts prevent overflow before the final int result.
walkthrough: For "1213", the valid tokenizations are 1|2|1|3,12|1|3,1|21|3,1|2|13 and 12|13. There are five, so return 5.
edgeCases: A leading zero has no decoding.
Zero can occur only within a valid pair such as 10 or 20.
Each digit must belong to exactly one token.
